newsitem.title: UK: British water cos told to invest more, boost image.
newsitem.headline: British water cos told to invest more, boost image.

text.p: British water and sewage companies were warned by the country's Environment Agency on Thursday that they needed to invest more and boost public confidence.
In a speech to a conference on the industry organised by The Economist magazine, the Environment Agency's head Ed Gallagher said the industry "must get the public back on its side."
He said the alienation of the public since privatisation in 1990 through a number of public relations disasters meant people would be less willing now to help companies by conserving water.

"Although the water companies' millions are crucial to environmental improvements, public behaviour has an almost equally important part to play," he told the conference on "Water industry -- Challenges & Opportunities."
Gallagher said some companies should consider whether staff cuts have actually improved productivity or "in reality lowered standards to an unacceptable level."

He pointed to leakage rates, which range from 10-30 percent, the need for repairs to raw sewage outlets and the high level of prosecutions for pollution incidents as factors undermining public confidence.
There have been 250 successful prosecutions of water companies for environmental damage since privatisation, equivalent to one every two or three weeks, he said.
Water companies have also been slammed for failing to maintain supplies during last summer's drought while high salaries to directors have exacerbated public anger.
Gallagher said perhaps the biggest disappointment since privatisation was "the alienation of the public" caused by such events.

He said that in the drought of 1976, 80 percent of people stopped watering their gardens and 70 percent flushed their toilets less. "There are few who would believe the public would act in the same way today," he said.
